name: InvokeAI
tagline: Text-to-image on a card you own, with the checkpoint, the gallery and the electricity bill all in one building.

local.note: This runs on the NVIDIA card in the computer you are sitting at, which is where a studio you sit in front of belongs, so the only things it costs you are the disk your gallery fills and a machine that has to be awake while you work.

quote.text: Enable multiuser support. When disabled, the application runs in single-user mode using a default system account with administrator privileges.

citations.claim: Upstream's own GitHub Actions workflow builds the container on every v*.*.* tag and pushes it to ghcr.io/invoke-ai/invokeai, for linux/amd64 only, because there are no pytorch builds for arm64 with CUDA.
Upstream's hardware table gives 8 GB of VRAM and 16 GB of system RAM as the floor for SDXL, and states that AMD GPUs are supported on Linux only.
InvokeAI runs single-user by default, with no accounts and every request served as an administrator; multiuser mode is one configuration flag away and is what this install turns on.
The image sets INVOKEAI_ROOT to /invokeai and INVOKEAI_PORT to 9090, and its entrypoint chowns that directory to the container user before dropping privileges to it.
The Stable Diffusion XL base checkpoint this install pins is published under the CreativeML Open RAIL++-M licence, is not gated, and its files have not changed since October 2023.

whatYouSignUpFor: The bill changes shape and, on rented hardware, goes up. This needs an NVIDIA card with 8 GB of memory and a machine with 16 GB of RAM, and a rented GPU instance costs several times a Midjourney Standard subscription every month whether you generate anything or not. This entry pays for itself on a desktop that already has the card in it. On a rented box, do the arithmetic before the install rather than after.

The pictures are the checkpoint, not the studio. InvokeAI is the canvas, the queue, the gallery and the model manager; what comes out is decided by the weights you install, and this one installs Stable Diffusion XL. That is a capable open model and it is not Midjourney v7. Anyone promising you the house style of a closed model on your own hardware is selling something.

You are agreeing to a model licence as well as a software one. InvokeAI itself is Apache-2.0. The SDXL base checkpoint is CreativeML Open RAIL++-M, which is use-restricted rather than open source: it permits commercial use and forbids a list of uses named in the licence. Read it once. Better checkpoints exist and several of the interesting ones are gated behind a Hugging Face account and terms you have to accept yourself.

Nobody is filtering your prompts, and nobody is filtering the output either. A hosted generator refuses things; this does not, because there is no policy layer between you and the model. That is the freedom people come here for and it is also the responsibility: what this machine produces is produced by you, on your hardware, under your name.

No community, no gallery, no other people's prompts to learn from. A large part of what a Midjourney subscription buys is the feed: thousands of images a day with their settings attached, and a Discord full of people who already solved the thing you are stuck on. Self-hosting gets you the generator and none of that.
